Chapter 7: Managing Expectations—Letting Go of Perfection and Comparison
Have you ever caught yourself holding your life up to a standard that just feels impossible? Maybe it’s your own expectations, or maybe it’s the pressures that seem to come from everyone around you—or even the world at large. The truth is, always chasing perfection, or constantly comparing ourselves to others, can quietly drain the joy out of even our brightest moments.
Think of managing expectations like adjusting the focus on a camera. When your expectations are too sharp, too rigid, the picture gets blurry and you miss what’s right in front of you. But if you gently bring things into focus, with a little compassion, suddenly, you start to appreciate life as it really is—instead of how you think it should be.
So, what does it actually look like to manage expectations in everyday life? Let’s break it down into a few simple practices.
First, try embracing the idea of “good enough.” That means allowing space for imperfection, both in yourself and in others. After all, growth isn’t about being flawless—it’s about making progress, one step at a time.
Next, watch out for the comparison trap, especially with social media. Whenever you notice yourself measuring your life against someone else’s highlight reel, take a breath and remember—everyone’s fighting their own hidden battles, even if you don’t see them.
Another powerful shift? Redefine what success means to you. Align your idea of achievement with your own values, not just what the outside world expects. What if your definition of success was simply living in a way that feels true to you?
And don’t forget to celebrate small wins. Those little moments of progress? They’re worth noticing and enjoying, instead of waiting for some big, far-off milestone to finally feel proud.
Let’s put this into perspective. Imagine a parent who feels pressure to create the perfect holiday for their family. They might get so caught up in the details that stress takes over, and the joy fades away. But if they shift their focus to just being together—sharing laughter, making memories—the whole experience becomes more real, more joyful, and a lot less stressful.
Letting go of perfection and comparison isn’t something you master overnight. It’s an ongoing process, one that calls for gentle reminders and a little self-forgiveness along the way. But with time, this shift opens up space for genuine happiness—happiness that’s rooted in accepting and being grateful for the present moment, just as it is.
